rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2013> three-season (2006/07<U+2013>2008/09) split-plot field experiment at Daxing, NCP, comparing level-basin (BI) and surface drip (DI) irrigation at four scheduling thresholds, with flow-metered irrigation amounts and TDR/gravimetric soil water. Q2: Table 4 and Table 9 <U+2013> seasonal irrigation amounts measured by flow meter; relative to B1, drip treatments D1<U+2013>D4 saved 14, 19, 35 and 35 % of irrigation water (yield decrease 5<U+2013>22 %); Results state D3 saved 35 % water during 2007<U+2013>2009 with only 13 % yield loss; Conclusions state DI could produce expected yields with less water than BI.
rows.notes: Comparator is level-basin (precision-levelled, diked basins), an improved surface/flood method rather than traditional flood irrigation, and savings are 14<U+2013>35 %, not 50 %. Q3: water saving rests on a single method (flow-metered applications, water balance); no independent second method. Q4: mechanism for DI advantage (uniform application, lower soil evaporation) is asserted, not measured; deep drainage estimated by a coefficient, not measured; soil water content was monitored but not used to quantify the water-saving pathway. Q5/Q6: one site, one soil, one crop and cultivar, plots 4.5<U+00D7>5 m. Q7: the stated condition (deficit irrigation) refers to DI's yield/WUE advantage, not to water saving as such; high wheat prices/reasonable water prices are mentioned for adoption, not as a requirement for the effect. Q8: limitations noted concern LAI measurement error and omission of system investment cost, not the water-saving result. Q9: only means and Duncan letters/F-tests; no SD, SE, CI or range reported for irrigation saved.

notes: Full text appears complete. Study is a 3-year plot experiment comparing surface drip with level-basin irrigation for winter wheat in the North China Plain; its own evidence is irrigation amounts, soil water, growth, yield, ETc and WUE.
